posts.cooked: Oh boy; this is one of the best episodes we’ve had in a while. I’m going to be pulling philosophical concepts and Justifications out of this episode for weeks. For now, all I’ll say is that the discussion of Entropy vs. Chaos unlocked one of the better explanations I’ve ever had of what Magic actually is, and why it needs to exist as a separate concept from Science (contrary to Clarke’s Law). The discussion of how these two concepts “feel different”, regardless of their meaning within physics, exactly represents the true source of magical power, which is the dimension of higher thought that the human mind reaches across to, while remaining anchored in the world of matter and energy and scientific fact.

posts.cooked:
The guise speech at the end really makes me think of Elan from Order of the Stick.

“You can become a better person. Robot. Spaceship. Sword. Whatever.”

This is not the end of the story…much like Thor Ragnarok. Sometimes it’s better to end.

Wagers Masters meeting within Hul would probably just drive them both insane, which is really something given that he wasn’t sane to begin with. As to why he follows his own rules, that’s obvious enough: you can’t have a wager if the parties to the bet aren’t forced to adhere to the terms of the bet. I can almost guarantee that the original primordial being of chaos, who came into being at the dawn of time, probably didn’t play cards or dice before any sapient life ever existed; likely that being somehow died and WM took its place.

On the list of villains who’d wish C&A I’ll, they forgot one: Hammer and Anvil would definitely kill them for having their faces!
